A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same research work, with 45 readable pages including Appendices A–F. Full text and rendered-page comparisons support reliable assessment; differences are confined to the first-page version stamp and the rendering of Figure 6.

before.justification: Section 5 and Appendix F report original simulation, ablation, robustness and real-video parameter-estimation results. Section 5.2.1 explicitly distinguishes the authors' OURS results from borrowed baseline results.

after.justification: The same original simulation and real-video results remain in Section 5 and Appendix F, including the authors' estimates in Table 5 and the nuisance experiments in Table 6.

M1.justification: The shared scalar-output CNN encoder, centered finite differences, ODE residual loss, variance-floor regularizer and multi-trajectory procedure are unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same pendulum, intensity and scale simulations across four damping regimes, clean real-video pendulums, wheel-mounted phone pendulum and synthetic nuisance scenarios.

E2.justification: Table 5 retains the same PAIG, NIRPI and LPFV comparators. Table 4 retains the same no-regularization, KL-regularization and variance-floor comparisons.

E3.justification: Section 5 and Appendix F retain identical experimental frame resolutions, sampling rates, initial conditions, clip durations, single- and multi-trajectory procedures, optimization settings and string-length RMSE evaluation.

E4.justification: The loss ablation, variance-floor sensitivity study, trajectory-duration and initial-condition sweeps, and four-category nuisance stress test are unchanged, including Tables 4 and 6–15.

E5.justification: Both versions report mean and standard deviation over five seeds for synthetic and wheel-pendulum experiments and over five clips for each clean-pendulum length. Figure 3 uncertainty bands and Table 6 per-seed reporting are unchanged.

E6.justification: Numerical entries and findings match throughout the main text and appendices. For example, Table 5 retains OURS RMSE values of 0.050, 0.070 and 0.101 m, and Section 5.2.2 retains the wheel-pendulum estimate 8.998 ± 0.009.

T1.justification: The state-consistency and slope-coverage definitions, identifiability theorems, finite-sample bounds, proofs, conditioning analysis and constant-term derivations in Sections 3–4 and Appendices A–E are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain identical claims about coverage-based identifiability, trajectory requirements, finite-sample guarantees and variance-floor regularization.

C2.justification: Interpretations of undamped recovery, regularization and LPFV comparisons are unchanged. Both versions retain the same state-consistency qualifications, nuisance failure conditions and limitations to scalar second-order LTI dynamics.

D1.justification: Appendix F retains identical architecture, learning-rate, initialization, preprocessing and nuisance-generation details. The code-access URL is unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited works, reference list and research positioning are identical, including the architectural relationship to LPFV and the emphasis on identifiability analysis.

P1.justification: The first-page arXiv stamp changes from v1 dated 27 May 2026 to v2 dated 31 July 2026. The title, authors, prose, terminology and section structure are otherwise unchanged.

P2.justification: Figure 6 on page 35 is downsampled from 3835 × 1031 to 2200 × 591 pixels and JPEG-compressed, with tiny placement shifts on that page. It depicts the same frames with the same labels and caption; other figures and tables are unchanged.

improvement.justification: The scientific content, evidence, reproducibility information and limitations are identical, including the appendices. The updated version stamp and lower-resolution Figure 6 do not meaningfully affect clarity or evidential value; the figure remains legible and conveys the same information.
